name: Sunday Times cryptic crossword, Penguin book 1 No 29

clue.text: I’m about to enter easily managed home
Prohibit a couple of articles of fruit

Seen in the flesh only by the X-ray specialist ?
They’re made by temperamental people + playwrights included, of course

A wet kind of monarch — subject to pinching!
Only twenty, but apparently more mature than that — yet still liable to get paid off
The hand-over of French special clothing
Very, very frightened at hags’ riotous get-together!
Disappeared gradually when kind of ripe and fallen off
Supporter of women’s rights displays short skirt in a half- safe street
Pastry brought to City of London district by rail perhaps
Diminishes hunger with a dish of sausages!
They rise in anger
She fashions stuff from minerals in trains
Title all right for composer
As miserable as a diver?
Doctor joins the girls —- how sweet! .. .
...and an ungentlemanly fellow joins the Engineers — how select!
‘Why shouldst thou, but for some felonious end, in thy dark — thus close up the stars’ (Milton: Comus)
As Jack does it?
To walk over the heather like this is really nonsensical
Without the usual means of support
Song about chaps from a particular republic
Fatter in the pantry?
End your life in one of Australia’s extremities ~ farewell!
